WE ARE CLOSING THE RESTAURANT

…Just for tonight 9/6 & Sunday 9/7!

Hi everyone this is Bev, Chef-Owner here.  So I just got back from a much-needed vacation & it gave me more time to reflect on where I want to take the direction of the restaurant.

As many of you know, I am gearing up to open my bar in Nutley, Bevs @bevs_nj which is a full-circle moment for me within this industry.  For all that I’ve accomplished in the last 15 years I can say that I never want to stop learning, and never want to stop growing.  Facing challenging moments on a regular basis always serves as an opportunity to learn & grow through adversity.

Let’s be real here—this summer was less than ideal for myself and many others in this business and industry.  But it’s really just caused me to figure out how to come out of it and embrace whatever challenges have come my way.  My solution:  a full menu overhaul.  New concept.  More pocket-friendly prices.  More family-friendly options.  More cooking of food that I love making & sharing with everyone who has believed in me and my business for the last 3.5 years. 

The menu will reflect a more relaxed, casual approach that honestly aligns with what we are trying to do at Bevs.  I want Walnut St. Kitchen to be everyone’s neighborhood joint for a quick, solid, affordable dinner that you can bring your kids to without all the fuss.  So much of our clientele are parents/new parents that just want to enjoy dinner with being comfortable bringing their kids.  I want your kids to grow up in this neighborhood remembering going out to dinner at WSK.  We want to grow with you and your family. ❤️❤️

In any event, we will be back at it on Tuesday 9/9.  Cause there ain’t no rest for the wicked. 

Okay bye love you all!

That’s right, I’m actually going on a vacation, and yes I do deserve it and also desperately need one! 

Wow EDIT:  it should say 9/5, but I’m tired and delirious so everyone leave me alone now thanks!! See you next year 🙃

Sorry to anyone who wanted to come in this week, but you guys had all summer to pop your pretty little heads in!  Mommy needs a break from working 18+ hour days 🫠

Our bagel shop @walnutstreetbagelsandco will continue to be open except for Tuesday 9/2.

We hope you all have a wonderful LDW & we look forward to welcoming everyone back in for dinner next weekend!

Lately, I’ve been sitting with the idea that love shouldn’t wait.

Not for milestones. Not for grief. Not for someday.

I’m deeply grateful for friendships rooted in consistency, care, and gentleness—friendships that remind me of my worth and show me that love doesn’t only live in romance.

It lives in showing up. It lives in pouring into one another. It lives in giving flowers while people are still here to receive them—literally and metaphorically. 💐

I truly love all my friends so this certainly isn’t dig at anyone, but these three have consistently shown up for me during one of my toughest seasons. I’m especially thankful for Flisadam (@flisadamp ), Desiree (@deshadley ) and Robeana (@_beehumbled ) whose presence, hearts, and selflessness mean more to me than words can fully hold.

This is your reminder that strong friendships are a form of real love. 💖

Love your people out loud (love on your friends like you love on that man girl!). Show up in the moment.
Pour into those who pour into you.

If this resonated, let it move you—send a message, make the call, or give someone their flowers today (while they can smell and appreciate them). 💐 #FriendshipAppreciation 💕💕

Anna is living the contented life of a literary widow, enjoying her husband’s royalty checks in perpetuity. But when she publishes her own book, she receives excerpts of a novel she never expected to see again. Something has gone very wrong, and someone out there knows far too much. With her signature wit, Korelitz gives readers an antihero to root for while satirizing the world of publishing in this deliciously fun and suspenseful read.

What a fantastic night!! I attended a wine and food pairing dinner at the Turtle And The Wolf Restaurant in Montclair, NJ.  Gary’s Buy-Rite in Wayne teamed up with Shafer wines from Napa Valley  for this delicious meal and wonderful evening!

We tasted 6 wines:

1. Red Shoulder Ranch Chardonnay 2022- honeycomb, white flowers, apricot and pineapple. 
2. TD-9 Cabernet Sauvignon 2022 - ripe plum, violet, red & black cherries and rhubarb. A blend of 75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 18% Merlot, 4% Malbec and 3% Petit Verdot. My favorite of the evening! 
3. One Point Five Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 - red plum, black cherry, coffee, cassis.  A blend of 92% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Petit Verdot, 3% Merlot and 2% Malbec. 
4. Relentless Syrah 2019 - meatiness, black plum, dark chocolate, blackberry, spice. 
5. Hillside Select Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 - black cherry, black currant, leather, black tea. 
6. Hillside Select Cabernet Sauvignon 2019 - blackberry, cassis, forest floor, spice.

I think I need to go back to Napa soon to visit this winery! 🍷🍇✈️

A longstanding favorite of mine, Turtle and The Wolf has been a staple in our community. The owners (Lauren Hirschberg and Matt Trevenen) were raised in Montclair, and the name is also derived from the town. The turtle and wolf were two of the clan symbols for the Lenape Indians. As these were the indigenous people to the area that is now Montclair. 

Turtle and The Wolf serves American Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal ingredients sourced as locally as possible, when possible.

It is one not to miss, and a perfect place to cozy up and enjoy a warm meal as the winter months approach! 

📍 622 Valley Road, Upper Montclair

🚧 VET YOUR CONTRACTOR 🚧

This is how we vet our contractors in real time.

In construction and development, process beats promises every time.

What we look for is a clear, transparent process that establishes a real bid. Not guesses, not emotions, not shortcuts.

🚩 Red flag:
If a contractor feels threatened by competing bids, that tells you everything you need to know.
Strong operators don’t fear competition they stand on their numbers and their work and the cheapest contractor is not the best bid.

🧰 The truth:
All contractors are different. Each has their own lane, expertise, and strengths. The best ones know exactly where they add value and where they don’t.

🗣️ Communication is non-negotiable:
A quality contractor can:
✔️ Explain their scope clearly
✔️ Provide guidance, not confusion
✔️ Advise you like a partner, not just a vendor
✔️ Protect your downside, not just chase the job

This is how you de-risk projects, protect capital, and build long-term relationships not expensive lessons.

💡 Vet the process.
💡 Vet the mindset.
💡 Vet the communication.

Tough GBs build tough players. I believe I took this drill from Coach Torpey awhile back. A great drill to get the juices flowing and build some competition in practice. It’s a 3v3 gb with everyone on the outside keeping the ball in play. Our one rule is you must complete one pass. 

This develops a ton of skills including contested gbs, handling pressure, moving the ball off the ground, and getting open off ball. As a defense it gives us opportunities to double the ball and build on our ability to play two defensively which is arguably one of the most important skills a defender can have. 

We allow creativity when it comes to passing and finishing in this drill. Small part drills are a great time for players to experiment with BTB, lever passes, leaners, and twisters.

In construction and development, process beats promises every time.

🚩 Red flag:
If a contractor feels threatened by competing bids, that tells you everything you need to know.
Strong operators don’t fear competition they stand on their numbers and their work and the cheapest contractor is not the best bid.

🧰 The truth:
All contractors are different. Each has their own lane, expertise, and strengths. The best ones know exactly where they add value and where they don’t.

🗣️ Communication is non-negotiable:
A quality contractor can:
✔️ Explain their scope clearly
✔️ Provide guidance, not confusion
✔️ Advise you like a partner, not just a vendor
✔️ Protect your downside, not just chase the job

Among the many incredible pieces, the work of Youngha형 truly left me in awe. He interviewed two North Korean defectors and wove their stories into symbolic elements, embedding them in stained glass — a reflection of their new lives as Christians in Korea. As the light pours through, their journeys cast vivid colors onto the floor like a path of resilience and freedom.

It’s more than art — it’s storytelling through light, faith, and survival. Truly unforgettable. 🖤

After the exhibition, we headed to Nami Nori, the place Youngha형 said he absolutely wanted to try while in New York. Thanks to Chef Jihan, we had such a joyful meal — the perfect way to end an inspiring day.

Did you know that the beloved Christmas ⛄ classic "It's a Wonderful Life" has deep New Jersey roots?

The story began with Philip Van Doren Stern, a Jersey City native, Lincoln High School alum, and 1924 Rutgers graduate. He dreamed up "The Greatest Gift" in the late 1930s, self-printed it as a 1943 Christmas card pamphlet, and sent it to friends which eventually reached Frank Capra and became the iconic film starring Jimmy Stewart

The original tale was inspired by the charming town of Califon in Hunterdon County, complete with its historic iron bridge (the spot where the protagonist contemplates jumping, before his guardian angel steps in)

When you see the town of Bedford Falls next time you watch this movie, remember, it has a lot of Jersey in it

Also, I (Jim) debated going full cornball with this post... and I ultimately landed on "yes, yes I will"... so I am gonna get a bit melodramatic and nostalgic on you guys to explain 📷#2, so bare with my story time .. 😅

*20*‼️years ago, back in 2006, when I was a much younger, much larger, very awkward high schooler, I was already very much into playing music, but had yet to partake in any kind of local scene. That all changed when I stepped foot into a local church basement venue in my hometown, called "Sacred Grounds". The first time I went to Sacred Grounds, I saw some cool bands, but no other act stood out to me more than Team Goldie. At the time, he was just one guy, an iPod, and a dream. 

Not only did Team Goldie command everyone's attention the second he took the stage, but he did it with such confidence and such a cool factor. My young, awkward self immediately admired and aspired to be that cool. It helped that his songs were incredible, too. Quirky, insanely catchy pop-punk mixed with hip-hop flair that easily rivaled any MySpace-era hits of that time. Needless to say, seeing Team Goldie back then is what inspired me to keep coming back to local venues and searching for more of that spirit and energy. Partaking in said local music community led to so many friendships, connections and memories that I still cherish to this day. 

Years went on, and I was in a couple bands that shared amazing bills with Team Goldie. Some time after that, I took a break from music, and Team Goldie also took a hiatus. So, if you had told awkward high school me back in 2006 that 20 ‼️ years later, I would still be playing shows, AND would get the chance to perform with Team Goldie on a bill again, I would've told you that you were full of it. 

And yet! Here we are! Make plans to come out to this one!! 📆

Neither option is “right” or “wrong”. You CHOOSE what is best for YOU. 

And understand- how you feel AFTER is YOUR responsibility. It’s a decision YOU make. 

IMO, you can have best of both worlds❤️ but what you do 80% of the time (all year round) is what is most important to focus on. Not what happens in one week.
